title: Plus or Minus? Quadrant Signs Explained Simply | PUC Maths Class 11
description:
Spin a bicycle wheel and watch the tyre valve: sometimes above the hub, sometimes below, sometimes left, sometimes right. Diya asks a simple question: when the valve is below the hub, is its height a minus number? In this animated lesson for PUC and Class 11 Maths (NCERT Chapter 3, Trigonometric Functions) we find out why sin, cos and tan are plus in some quadrants and minus in others.

You will watch the point P travel round the unit circle while the graph of y = sin x draws live beside it, see the signs of cos and sin change quadrant by quadrant, derive the signs of tan, cosec, sec and cot, and remember the whole table with All, Sine, Tangent, Cosine. Two pause-and-think questions, a worked example (sin = 3/5 in quadrant II), the exam trap about tan in quadrant III, an original JEE Main pattern question with a full solution, a recap card and three questions to check yourself.

Made for PUC (Karnataka), CBSE Class 11 and JEE Main students.

In this video:
0:00 The tyre valve: above or below?
0:28 Recall: the unit circle
0:56 Live: P goes round, sin x draws itself
1:39 Signs of tan, cosec, sec and cot
2:15 60 degrees vs 120 degrees
2:52 All, Sine, Tangent, Cosine
3:37 Worked example: sin = 3/5 in quadrant II
4:20 Exam trap: tan in quadrant III
4:37 Where it is asked
4:45 Practice question (JEE Main pattern)
5:23 Recap and three questions to answer

Next episode (Ep 29): Domain and Range of Trigonometric Functions. The valve can never rise higher than the wheel's radius, so how big can sin x ever get?

Video by Quest Academy.
